title: KPI Edge Buffering and Delta Telemetry for Inference Pipelines
creator: Leah Kim
description: Implement a resilient edge-side buffering and delta-encoding layer for inference KPIs to reduce traffic to the central metrics pipeline, preserve SLO-aligned observability, and attach trace context for per-request attribution. This ticket covers the collection-side changes that run on Dedicated/Private inference nodes (sidecar or lightweight agent) and the downstream compatibility hooks required for Prometheus scrape adapters and OTLP exporters. The goal is to: (1) persist short-term metric batches on local disk during network partitions, (2) emit delta-encoded counters and compact histograms to cut cardinality and egress cost, (3) attach sparse exemplars / trace IDs for latency/error buckets to enable trace->metric linking, and (4) provide configurable watermarks for prefixed KV-cache metrics so we do not duplicate tokens across retransmits.
acceptance_criteria: Edge agent persists up to 2GB of telemetry on local disk and recovers after restart without duplicate ingestion
Delta-encoded counters and histogram deltas are accepted by central OTLP gateway and mapped to Prometheus-compatible time series with no data loss
Exemplars containing trace IDs are present for P50/P95/P99 latency buckets for 95% of sampled requests
End-to-end tests demonstrate that network partitions of up to 60s do not cause >5% spike in central downstream QPS when using buffering + delta encoding
Dashboard panels (inference-latency/cost-per-token) reflect consistent values within 1% variance compared to baseline telemetry during normal conditions
comments: 2025-02-12 Leah Kim: Created ticket. Problem observed: dedicated nodes at edge regions occasionally spike egress and Prometheus scrape timeouts during bulk KV-cache flushes. Proposal: local buffering + delta encoding + exemplar enrichment.

2025-02-14 Ravi Sharma: Design review with infra and runtime teams. Agreed on sidecar approach to avoid recompiling runtime; sidecar will use append-only segment files for durability. We will reuse the existing OTLP exporter codepath and add a delta layer.

2025-02-18 Marco Ruiz (runtime): Raised concern about double-counting if sidecar retransmits counters after partial ack. Action: include monotonic window sequence numbers to deduplicate at ingest gateway.
2025-02-20 Design review: Decided exemplar format will be 'trace_id:span_id' and attached to histogram exemplars only when sample_rate >= 0.01. Added gating flag for high-cardinality workloads.
2025-02-24 QA: Initial integration tests passing for small load. Observed 40% reduction in egress bytes for metric-heavy workloads with delta encoding enabled.
2025-02-28 Ravi Sharma: Implemented dedupe window and prometheus adapter changes; opening PR: https://github.com/redwood/realtime-telemetry/pull/891
monitoring_queries: Deduplication: use sequence_number + node_id to filter repeated batches at ingest layer
rollout_plan: canary: enable on 5 dedicated nodes in us-west-2 with sample_rate=0.05 and disk_quota=500MB
monitor: watch egress_bytes_total, scrape_errors_total, and downstream ingestion latency for 24h
scale: increase rollout to remaining dedicated nodes if no regressions after 72h
fallback: sidecar exposes admin endpoint to drain and disable buffering; central gateway will accept raw counters if needed
